outcome: mode of delivery (VBAC vs. repeat LSCS)
cohort: The study included 284 pregnant women, at a gestational age of over 35 weeks, with a history of previous Caesarean Section.
finding: Ultrasonographic evaluation of LSCS scar features (triangular shape, thickness >3mm, continuous, hyperechoic) plays a critical role in predicting delivery outcomes, with specific features associated with higher VBAC success and others with higher repeat CS rates.
mod_finding: Triangular scars and thicker scars (>3 mm) were associated with higher success rates for VBAC, while ballooning patterns and thinner scars (<3 mm) were linked to higher rates of repeat CS, and continuous scars were linked to successful VBAC.
cross-section timing: Between February 2022 and January 2025, when pregnant women were at a gestational age of over 35 weeks.
